clips.send: Buoyancy. The upward push of a liquid. A liquid pushes up on anything placed in it. This upward push is the buoyant force. The buoyant force equals the weight of the liquid the object pushes aside (displaces). An object less dense than the liquid floats; one that is denser sinks. A floating object sinks only deep enough to displace its own weight — the less dense it is, the higher it rides (look at the ping-pong ball).

clips.send: Common mix-up: “Heavy things sink and light things float” is wrong! What matters is whether the object’s density is greater or less than the liquid’s. A big log is heavy but floats; a small steel nut is light but sinks.

clips.send: Density. Mass per unit volume. Density equals mass divided by volume (D equals m divided by V). Units: g/ cubic centimeters (the same as g/mL). It tells how tightly matter is packed — how much mass is squeezed into each cubic centimeters . Density is a physical property: each pure substance has its own density, which helps identify it. Cutting an object in half halves both the mass and the volume, so its density stays the same.

clips.send: 密度。单位体积的质量。密度 等于 质量 除以 体积（ρ 等于 m 除以 V），常用单位 g/ 立方厘米 （与 g/mL 相同）。密度表示物质有多“紧密”——每立方厘米里装了多少质量。密度是物质的物理性质：每种纯净物都有自己的密度，可以用来鉴别物质。把物体切成两半，质量和体积都减半，所以密度不变。

clips.send: 浮力。液体对物体向上的托力。液体会对浸在其中的物体产生向上的托力，这就是浮力。浮力等于物体排开的液体所受的重力。物体的密度小于液体就上浮，大于液体就下沉。漂浮的物体只沉到排开液体的重力等于自身重力为止——密度越小，露出液面越多（看看乒乓球）。
